# AGENTS.md (.github)

This directory contains GitHub configuration and CI workflows.

## Workflow inventory

| Workflow | Trigger | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `apple-builds.yml` | push/PR to `main` | macOS build+test (incl. wallet trait), iOS + visionOS cross-compile of the umbrella scheme, tvOS cross-compile of the BitcoinKernel scheme only, DocC validation for Bitcoin + BitcoinKernel |
| `tuist-apps.yml` | push/PR to `main` | Build + test the Tuist demo apps (`NodeApp`, `KernelApp`) on macOS and the iOS Simulator via `xcodebuild build-for-testing`/`test-without-building` on the Tuist-generated workspace (matrix: app × platform) |
| `docker-builds.yml` | push/PR to `main` | Linux build+test via `docker build .` |
| `docc-release.yml` | release published or manual | Matrix build of DocC archives (Bitcoin + BitcoinKernel), upload to release assets |
| `flake-hunt.yml` | manual only | Repeat one demo app's test bundle N times on CI hardware to hunt (or disprove) an intermittent failure. Never runs on push or PR. |
| `development-docs.yml` | push/PR to `main`, only when `Development/**`, `.vale.ini`, `.vale/**` or the workflow itself changes | Unit-test the checker in `Development/Tools`, verify every plan and decision record's frontmatter and that the generated index tables are current (`plans --check`), lint plan structure with Vale, and print document lengths as advisory output. Runs on `macos-26` because Swift ships preinstalled; never builds the package itself. |

**Platform coverage (package)**: macOS (build+test), iOS (build only), visionOS (build only), tvOS (BitcoinKernel only — `Bitcoin` depends on `bitcoind`'s `execvp()` call which is `__TVOS_PROHIBITED`). Linux via Docker. watchOS is blocked by additional POSIX prohibitions (`fork`, `execvp`, etc.) and not in the matrix.

**Platform coverage (demo apps)**: `tuist-apps.yml` builds and tests `NodeApp` and `KernelApp` on macOS and the iOS Simulator. visionOS (both apps) and tvOS (`KernelApp` only, by the same `execvp()` constraint) are staged as commented matrix rows.

## Boundaries (strict)

- Do not broaden GitHub Actions `permissions` without a clear justification.
- Do not print or log secrets/tokens.
- Do not add new third-party actions without asking.

## Workflow conventions

- **Least-privilege pattern for private repos**: set `permissions: {}` at the **workflow** level (deny-by-default baseline for any job that omits its own block) and grant the **minimum** each job needs at the job level. For `actions/checkout` against a private repo, that minimum is `contents: read`. A bare `permissions: {}` at the job level strips `contents: read` and causes `actions/checkout` to fail with a 404 "repository not found" error on private repos.
- A failing `tuist-apps.yml` job uploads Xcode's test record (`.xcresult`) as a downloadable artifact. The step MUST carry `if: failure()` — a step with no condition is *skipped* once an earlier step failed, i.e. exactly when the record matters. One record per retry attempt (xcodebuild refuses an existing bundle path) and one artifact name per matrix row (concurrent rows otherwise collide). Verified end-to-end on a throwaway branch, not assumed.
- Intermittent failures: reach for `flake-hunt.yml` before theorising. One clean run proves little — at the ~1-in-30 rate seen in run 32344108476, 50 clean iterations is 82% confidence but 100 is 97%. The iteration-count arithmetic is in the workflow file; do not lower the default without redoing it. `-retry-tests-on-failure` is deliberately never used: it re-runs failures and hides what you are hunting.
- Workflows use `env:` blocks for context values — no inline `${{ }}` interpolation in `run:` scripts.
- Avoid fragile shell output capture for UTF-8 / multiline content; prefer temp files and tools like `jq` reading from files.
- swift-bitcoinkernel gates dev plugins (`swift-plugin-tuist`, `swift-plugin-subtree`, `swift-docc-plugin`) behind `Context.gitInformation?.currentTag` — see `Package.Dependency.developmentDependencies` in `Package.swift`, which returns an empty array when the package is resolved at a tagged ref. Consumers of tagged releases don't download dev tooling. Workflows that need those plugins (e.g. `docc-release.yml` invoking `swift package generate-documentation`) currently check out at the release tag, which excludes the plugin; if DocC generation regresses at tag time, this is the likely cause and the workaround is to delete the local tag before running the plugin, or to pin the plugin outside `developmentDependencies`. `tuist-apps.yml` also needs `swift-plugin-tuist`, but it runs only on push/PR to `main` (untagged), so the gate never strips it there.

## Gotchas

- The private-repo `permissions: {}` failure mode (404 on checkout) only surfaces on GitHub runners, not locally. Always push a test branch to verify permission changes.
- `docc-release.yml` uses a matrix strategy (`[Bitcoin, BitcoinKernel]`) with a separate `release` job for artifact collection. Adding a new DocC target requires updating both the matrix list and the `release` job's download+upload steps.
- The umbrella scheme (`BitcoinKernel-Package`) builds both products. On tvOS it fails because the `Bitcoin` product transitively uses `execvp()`; the tvOS job uses the per-product `BitcoinKernel` scheme to skip `Bitcoin`. Do not switch the tvOS job back to the umbrella scheme without first guarding the `execvp()` call (or removing the dependency on it) in `Sources/bitcoind/src/util/exec.cpp`. watchOS is similarly blocked and would also need `fork`/`exec` guards in vendored C++ sources.
- `tuist-apps.yml` builds the demo apps, whose dependency graph combines the root package with `Projects/Project.swift`'s `swift-tor` pin. Shared transitive deps (notably `swift-event`) MUST resolve to one version, or `tuist generate` fails before any build. This bit us once: root moved to `swift-event` 0.2.1 (PR #17) while `swift-tor` 0.1.0 still pinned 0.1.4; fixed by bumping the Tor pin to 0.1.1. When bumping `swift-event` in root, confirm the pinned `swift-tor` release agrees.
- `tuist-apps.yml` drives builds/tests with `xcodebuild` **directly** on the Tuist-generated workspace, NOT `tuist xcodebuild`. The `swift package tuist …` plugin forwards args verbatim to the tuist binary, but SwiftPM's own CLI parser first reads xcodebuild's single-dash long flags as short-flag clusters — `-workspace`/`-scheme` contain `-c`, which swallows the next token as a `--configuration` value — and `--` leaks straight through to xcodebuild ("Unknown build action"). So `swift package tuist xcodebuild build-for-testing -scheme …` cannot work; use Tuist only for `generate`, then `xcodebuild build-for-testing`/`test-without-building -workspace Projects/Bitcoin.xcworkspace -scheme <App> …`. (The `swift-plugin-tuist` 4.195.11 pin in `Package.swift` is kept for the newer toolchain; this workflow does not depend on it.)
- libbitcoinkernel has process-global state (the `BCLog` logger singleton, `cs_main`, the global chainstate) that isn't safe under swift-testing's in-process parallelism. This is handled **in test code**, not with `--no-parallel`: (1) any test that creates a `Context`/`ChainstateManager` or mutates the global logger carries the `.kernelSerialized` trait (`Tests/BitcoinKernelTests/Support/KernelSerialization.swift`) — a `TestScoping` trait whose shared `AsyncSemaphore` serializes those tests against each other across all files and suites, while everything else stays parallel (`.serialized` can't do this — it only orders tests within one suite). (2) The Esplora `BlockSource` tests inject an in-memory `MockHTTPClient` (`HTTPDataFetching`) instead of stubbing `URLProtocol`, so they hold no global state and touch no network — a prior `URLProtocol`-interception-fails → real-DNS → retry path made them hang. So CI runs the package as ONE parallel `swift test`, plus a SECOND invocation that isolates the `Bitcoin Integration` daemon suite (`BitcoinTests.BitcoinTests/`) in its own process — the embedded `bitcoind`'s `StartLogging` and a kernel `LoggingConnection`'s `StartLogging` both `assert(m_buffering)` on the one global `LogInstance` and can't share a process (the original `--traits wallet` SIGABRT). The one exit test (`#expect(processExitsWith:)` — `bestEntryTrapsWhenRecoverySkipped`, which guards the #35293 null-deref: it verifies the wrapper traps cleanly instead of SIGSEGV-ing in C) carries `.tags(.exitTest)` + `.enabled(if: ProcessInfo…environment["RUN_EXIT_TESTS"] != nil)`, so it auto-skips in CI and runs on demand via `RUN_EXIT_TESTS=1 swift test --no-parallel`. Exit tests can't run under the parallel runner (the spawn hangs amid the pool) or be `--filter`-isolated (the child re-enters the filtered run and recurses, which SE-0008 forbids), so a full unfiltered serial pass is the only way. Net: two invocations in `apple-builds.yml` + `Dockerfile`. The Tuist demo-app test bundles need the same protection and get it by *referencing* `Tests/BitcoinKernelTests/Support/{KernelSerialization,AsyncSemaphore}.swift` via relative paths in `Projects/Project.swift` rather than duplicating them — so a fix lands once. (Measured: with the reindex race fixed, 100 iterations found zero failures from suite overlap alone, so the trait is defence-in-depth there, not the thing that fixed run 32344108476.) New kernel-touching tests must carry `.kernelSerialized`; new exit tests must carry `.tags(.exitTest)` + the `.enabled(if:)` gate (do NOT add them to a `--skip` list — the gate handles it). Reserve exit tests for guards whose failure mode is memory-unsafety, not every `precondition`.
- `tuist-apps.yml`'s iOS rows retry `tuist test` (up to 5×, gated on a crash signature). The iOS-simulator test host intermittently segfaults at launch inside Apple's `UIApplicationMain` prep — `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` in `CFBundleGetIdentifier` / `_UIKitUserDefaults` → `NSUserDefaults` init — before our code or the test runner attaches, surfacing as `Early unexpected exit … test runner crashed before establishing connection`, not a test failure. The crash report has zero frames from our targets: an Apple/CoreSimulator launch race (~5-10% per launch locally, higher under CI load), reproduced with a clean cache. `--retry-count` can't help (it retries tests that ran; here the host died pre-connection), so the loop re-invokes `tuist test` to relaunch. The retry fires ONLY on that signature — any other non-zero exit fails fast — and macOS rows are single-attempt, so a genuine regression is never masked.

## Validation

- **macOS**: two invocations (see Gotchas) — `swift test --skip 'BitcoinTests\.BitcoinTests/'` (package, parallel; kernel-state tests gated by `.kernelSerialized`) · `swift test --filter 'BitcoinTests\.BitcoinTests/'` (embedded-bitcoind suite, isolated), each also run with `--traits wallet`. The #35293 exit test runs on demand via `RUN_EXIT_TESTS=1 swift test --no-parallel`.
- **Linux**: `docker build .`
- **iOS cross-compile**: `xcrun xcodebuild -skipMacroValidation -skipPackagePluginValidation build -scheme "BitcoinKernel-Package" -destination generic/platform=iOS`
- **visionOS cross-compile**: same as iOS, substitute `generic/platform=visionOS`
- **tvOS cross-compile (BitcoinKernel only)**: same shape, but use `-scheme "BitcoinKernel"` and `generic/platform=tvOS`. The umbrella scheme fails on tvOS — see Gotchas.
- **DocC validation**: `swift package generate-documentation --target Bitcoin --analyze --warnings-as-errors` (repeat for `BitcoinKernel`)
- **Tuist demo apps**: `swift package --disable-sandbox tuist generate -p Projects/ --no-open`, then `swift package --disable-sandbox tuist test <NodeApp|KernelApp> -p Projects/ --platform <macos|ios>`
- **Planning documents**: `swift test --package-path Development/Tools` (checker unit tests) · `swift run --package-path Development/Tools plans --check` (frontmatter valid, indexes current; omit `--check` to rewrite them) · `vale Development/` (plan structure). All three are fast and need no package build.
